Risk Assessment & Method Statement

On-Site IT Services, Equipment Collection & Secure Data Destruction

1. Legislative Framework

This RAMS complies with:
  • Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
  • Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999
  • Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992
  • Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER)
  • Display Screen Equipment Regulations 1992
  • Electricity at Work Regulations 1989
  • Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH)
  • HSE Management Standards for Work-Related Stress

2. Scope of Work

This RAMS covers standard on-site IT services including:

  • Collection of IT equipment (laptops, desktops, servers, peripherals)
  • On-site hardware diagnostics and repair
  • Data destruction and media sanitization
  • Network infrastructure assessment
  • Equipment transportation and secure storage
  • Remote technical support (where applicable)

3. Hazard Identification & Control Measures

3.1 Physical Hazards

Hazard Risk Control Measures
Manual Handling Medium Assess load before lifting. Use proper technique (bend knees, keep back straight). Request assistance for items >15kg. Use trolley/sack truck for bulk collections.
Electrical Safety Medium Visual inspection before handling. Do not handle visibly damaged equipment while powered. Isolate power before internal work. PAT-tested equipment only.
Driving for Work Medium Pre-journey vehicle checks (brakes, lights, tyres). Avoid driving when fatigued. Plan routes to avoid congestion. Mobile phone use prohibited while driving. Regular breaks on journeys >2 hours.
Sharps/Broken Equipment Low Wear protective gloves when handling damaged devices. Inspect equipment before packing. Report damaged items to client.
Slips, Trips, Falls Low Assess site conditions on arrival. Keep work area clear. Use appropriate footwear. Report hazards to site manager.
Display Screen Equipment Low Limit continuous screen work to 50-minute intervals during extended diagnostics. Adjust workstation for ergonomic posture.
COSHH (Chemicals) Low Thermal paste, cleaning solvents, and isopropyl alcohol handled with nitrile gloves. MSDS reviewed for unfamiliar products. Adequate ventilation ensured.
Vehicle Loading Low Park on level ground. Use vehicle handbrake. Load evenly to maintain balance. Secure items with straps to prevent movement.

3.2 Data & Security Hazards

Hazard Risk Control Measures
Data Security High Chain of custody maintained at all times. Equipment secured in locked vehicle. NIST 800-88 sanitization applied to all storage media.
Cybersecurity Incident Medium Report any suspected breach immediately to client representative. Document incident details. Do not attempt to access client network credentials. Use secure VPN where remote access is required.
Theft/Loss Medium Equipment inventoried before and after collection. Unique asset tags or serial numbers recorded. Vehicle secured with alarm when unattended.

3.3 Psychosocial & Wellbeing Hazards

Hazard Risk Control Measures
Lone Working Medium Inform office of location and expected duration. Mobile phone carried at all times. Check-in protocol for extended visits (>2 hours). Controls align with HSE guidance INDG73 (Rev. 2025).
Work-Related Stress Low Manageable workload maintained. Clear communication channels with client. Flexibility to reschedule non-urgent work if capacity exceeded.

4. Dynamic Risk Assessment

On-Site Assessment Protocol

This RAMS is supplemented by dynamic risk assessment performed on-site. Additional hazards identified at client premises will be documented and addressed in real-time. Where site conditions deviate significantly, work will be paused until appropriate controls are implemented.

5. Personal Protective Equipment

Equipment When Required
Safety footwear (toe protection) All on-site collections
Protective gloves (nitrile) Handling damaged, unknown, or chemically-treated equipment
Hi-visibility vest Warehouse, industrial site, or loading bay visits
Safety glasses Work involving potential debris (e.g., damaged CRT monitors)

6. Emergency Procedures

Emergency Contact: Jake Fieldhouse | +44 7404 090458
  • Fire: Evacuate immediately via nearest exit. Do not retrieve equipment. Call 999 if required.
  • Injury: Administer first aid if trained and safe. Call 999 for serious injuries. Complete accident report.
  • Security/Cyber Incident: Cease operations immediately. Notify client representative. Document details.
  • Personal Safety Concern: Leave premises immediately. Contact emergency services if necessary.

7. Environmental Considerations

Waste Management Compliance
  • Environment Agency Waste Carrier License: CBDL620098
  • Zero Landfill policy: equipment refurbished, recycled, or responsibly disposed
  • Hazardous materials (batteries, CRTs, toner) handled by licensed partners
  • Waste Transfer Notes provided for every collection
  • WEEE Regulations 2013 compliance maintained throughout chain of custody
